does: Cooks washed rice in a measured amount of water in a covered pot until all the water is taken up, then leaves it covered off the heat so that the grains finish plump, tender and separate, or lightly sticky for a short-grain kind.
how: Wash the rice in several changes of cold water, swirling it, until the water is much less cloudy. Drain it well.
Put it in a pot with a tight lid and add the measured water. A short-grain rice takes a little less water than a long-grain one.
Bring it to the boil uncovered or just covered, then turn the heat to its lowest and cover tightly.
Leave the lid on and do not stir, so that the steam stays in.
Take it off the heat when the water has gone, and let it stand covered. Then fluff it with a fork, or fold it with a paddle.

cues.text: The bubbling goes quiet and the pot starts to hiss softly once the water is used up.
Small steam holes show on the surface and no water is left at the edge.
The grains are plump and tender, and a short-grain rice clings in a mass.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the lid again and again, so that the steam escapes and the top stays hard.
mistakes.fix: Leave the lid on from the moment the heat goes down until the rice has rested.

mistakes.mistake: Stirring, which releases starch and turns the rice gluey.
mistakes.fix: Do not stir. Fluff it with a fork only at the end.

mistakes.mistake: Using too much water, so that the rice turns soft and wet.
mistakes.fix: Measure the water against the rice, and use a little less for a short-grain kind.

comes_after.why: Washing takes off the loose starch that would make the rice gluey.
